PUBLIC ADVISORY 

In view of reports of a proposed march to Parliament by CJP on 20.07.2026 (Monday), Delhi Police hereby categorically clarifies  that no permission has been sought or granted for any such protest march/procession.

Prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS (erstwhile section 144 CrPC) is in force in the New Delhi District. *Accordingly, protest marches, processions, demonstrations and assemblies of five or more persons are strictly prohibited*, except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar,  with prior permission.

As Parliament session is commencing from 20 July, strict security arrangements are in place to ensure public safety, security of protectees, and the protection of vital government installations.

Any person violating these prohibitory orders shall be liable for prosecution under Section 223 BNS and other applicable provisions of law.

Delhi Police appeals to all citizens to respect the law, refrain from participating in any unauthorised gathering or march, and cooperate in maintaining public peace, safety and security.
@LtGovDelhi @DelhiPolice @CJP_for_India

body:
An Open Letter to the Jantar Mantar protestors:

My dear young friends,

I address you today not as a politician or an MP, but as someone deeply troubled by what is happening to your generation of young Indians.

This is personal for me. I was born to a middle-class family: my father was a salaried newspaper employee, my mother a homemaker, with three children to educate on one income. For a family like ours, merit was not a slogan. Scholarships, fair examinations, honest results — these were the only way one salary could carry three children's dreams. 

I went to school in Mumbai and Kolkata, to college here in Delhi, topped the University and earned admission into IIM — and chose instead to follow my passion for international affairs, in America, on a scholarship. Nothing was inherited; everything was earned by hard work and yes, Exams.

So I know that a fair, merit-based system is the only ladder for young people from lower and middle-income families to climb up. When that ladder is broken — papers leaked, examinations cancelled, trust destroyed — the children of the rich and powerful do not suffer. They have other ladders. It is your dreams, and your families' sacrifices (and tragically, in some homes, young lives themselves) that are betrayed.

To the young people gathered at Jantar Mantar, and those raising your voices peacefully across India: this country hears you. Your anger is not indiscipline — it is the anguish of a generation that did everything right and was still betrayed . You are not alone.

And to the millions of young Indians watching quietly: your generation is not a problem to be managed. You are the answer to India's future. Do not lose hope. This ladder will be rebuilt — by you, and by every Indian who stands with you.

To Shri Sonam Wangchuk-ji, my heartfelt appeal: please end your fast. You have awakened the conscience of the nation;  that is what a fast is meant to do. India needs your voice for the long road ahead. 

With Parliament in session again from Monday, we will have an opportunity to raise the students’ issues in the highest forum of our democracy. That’s where the problem should be addressed, not by fasting unto death. Please heed my plea. 

And finally, to the Government:  I respectfully urge you to reach out and engage in the dialogue our democracy owes its young citizens. That is not weakness; that is statesmanship.

NTA Declares Result of NEET (UG) 2026

11.21 lakh candidates qualify;
Results declared in time for counselling and Medical College Admissions;
Toppers from almost all States and Union Territories;
More than 58 per cent of qualified candidates are women;
Examination conducted in 13 languages

The National Testing Agency (NTA) declares the result of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Undergraduate), NEET (UG) 2026. The result has been declared in time so that the medical-admission and counselling calendar for candidates stays on track.

A total of close to 20 lakh candidates appeared for NEET (UG) 2026 at 5,440 centres in 551 cities in India and 14 cities abroad. 11.21 lakh candidates have qualified for admission to undergraduate medical, dental, AYUSH and allied programmes.
Scorecards of all candidates are available on the official website, https://t.co/ehHaUsaoU6. The full list of Top Rankers, State Toppers, category-wise toppers (SC, ST, OBC-NCL, Gen-EWS, PwBD and PwD), category-wise cut-off marks and language-wise participation is also being published on the NTA website.

Overview of the Candidates who appeared in NEET UG Exam on 21st June 2026
Close to 20 lakh candidates appeared and 11.21 lakh qualified. Candidates appeared from every State and Union Territory of the country, in 13 languages. More than 58 per cent of the qualified candidates are women. 

The majority of the top-performing candidates are between 17 and 19 years of age.
Profile of the Top Rankers
138 candidates scored above 690 marks out of 720. Of these:
•Over 93 per cent appeared for NEET (UG) for the first time.
•99 per cent are between 17 and 19 years of age.

Geographical Distribution
Qualified candidates have emerged from every one of the 36 States and Union Territories, ranging from over 1.7 lakh in Uttar Pradesh to 43 in Lakshadweep. State Toppers include Jigmet Yangchan Lamo (Ladakh, 530 marks), Dhruv Tripathi (Andaman and Nicobar Islands, 606 marks) and Fahmida Anees (Lakshadweep, 573 marks), and cover every North-Eastern State. 17 State Toppers scored 700 or above; 26 scored above 690.

The 138 top rankers come from 66 cities across the country. The Top 17 rankers who scored more than 705 marks span eight States, namely Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

Score Distribution and Highest Scorers
•19 candidates scored above 700 out of 720.
•1,492 candidates scored 650 and above.
•10,160 candidates scored 600 and above.
•90,780 candidates scored 500 and above.
The highest score of 715 out of 720 was obtained jointly by Aryan Gupta (Punjab) and Panshul Bansal (Haryana).
Category-wise Qualified Candidates
Registered, appeared and qualified figures are being published in full for General, Gen-EWS, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwBD, PwD and Third Gender candidates. Separate topper lists for each category are provided in the accompanying toppers document.

Category-wise qualified candidates:
•General: 2.91 lakh
•OBC-NCL: 5.12 lakh
•SC: 1.59 lakh
•ST: 63,716
•Gen-EWS: 95,026
•PwBD: 3,666
•PwD: 303
Category-wise cut-off marks and percentiles are being published simultaneously.

Participation and Qualification of Women Candidates
More than 58 per cent of all qualified candidates are women. Women also qualified at a higher rate than men: 56.8 per cent of women who appeared qualified, as against 55.1 per cent of men.
Languages of the Examination
NEET (UG) 2026 was conducted in 13 languages: Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu and English.

Process and Timeline of Result Declaration
The result was declared within time through re-engineering of the process, with stages designed to run in parallel rather than in sequence, and with the de-linking of OMR sheet challenge from answer key release. Each stage was completed in full and made available for candidate view:
•Provisional answer key published on 25 June 2026; challenge window open from 25 to 28 June 2026.
•Scanned OMR answer sheets and recorded responses displayed to candidates from 13 to 15 July 2026.
•Final answer key published on 16 July 2026; result declared on 16 July 2026.

Statutory FrameworkNTA conducts NEET (UG) under Section 14 of the NMC Act, 2019 and Section 14 of the NCISM Act, 2020, and for BHMS under the NCH, on the direction of the Hon’ble Supreme Court and with the approval of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Ministry of Education.
NTA’s mandate is to conduct the examination, declare the result on eligibility criteria provided by NMC, and issue the All-India Rank. Merit lists, category lists, domicile determination and counselling are the remit of the admitting/State authorities. NTA has no role in these.
NEET (UG) result data is also used for admission to https://t.co/P1QVj20987. (H) Nursing and to BVSc and AH under the 15% VCI quota. AACCC is the counselling authority for the All-India Quota in BAMS/BUMS/BSMS and BHMS.

Counselling and Candidate Advisory
Counselling for the All-India Quota in MBBS/BDS is conducted by the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC). State quotas are conducted by respective State authorities. Candidates should rely only on official websites: https://t.co/ehHaUsaoU6, https://t.co/Kql0EMCxDN and State counselling portals.
Candidates are cautioned against fraudulent calls, messages or websites offering admission, seat blocking or score improvement. NTA does not contact candidates seeking money or credentials. Suspicious communication may be reported at neetug2026@nta.ac.in or 011-40759000.

🤯 BIG | Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke leads his party to a massive protest on Day-3 at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.

In the video, Dipke can be heard warning the police, who are allegedly seeking Aadhar cards of protestors from the site. Dipke warned them to stop doing that.

In the presence of a massive crowd, Dipke was heard addressing the police.

On the other hand, Dipke was previously heard saying that he would be arrested. However, it has been two days since, and Dipke is still protesting and not being arrested.

Dipke was also heard to have invited farmers to protest and join in the Cockroaches’ movement. However, no farmers have turned out so far.

With the re-NEET examination successfully conducted, Dipke’s protest continues to seek accountability from the Government over the paper leaks.

body:
Latest Guardian Sob Story On Umar Khalid Is Another Indication That NEET Is Just A Mask

On 30th June, The Guardian published a sympathetic profile of Umar Khalid, presenting the accused in the larger conspiracy case related to the 2020 anti-Hindu Delhi Riots as one of India’s most prominent “political prisoners” and a victim of a government crackdown on dissent. Built around reflections on prison, fading hope, Dostoevsky and Bhagat Singh, the article largely avoided examining the prosecution’s case against him.

The article needs to be scrutinised not just for what it said, but also for what it deliberately left outside the frame. The publication came amid open support for Khalid from the leadership and supporters of the so-called Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), whose protests were launched around the NEET paper leak and youth issues. However, protesters and CJP supporters, both online and offline, have called for Umar Khalid to be freed.

Titled “‘Humanity is a privilege’: Umar Khalid on his six years in an Indian jail without trial”, The Guardian article was written by Hannah Ellis-Petersen, the publication’s Delhi correspondent who is known for her anti-India propaganda. In the article, she described Khalid as an activist, a left-wing rights campaigner and a fierce critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She claimed that he had become a symbol of the alleged weaponisation of the judicial system against government opponents.
author: AugadhBhudeva

body:
In a recent interview with Samdish Bhatia on Unfiltered by Samdish, Dipke claimed that he had kept his movement peaceful, Constitution-centric and difficult to discredit. Out of no where, Samdish remarked that his surname was not Khalid, to which Dipke said that had he been a Khalid, Saifi or Muslim, he would have been in jail. Through the remark, Dipke appeared to suggest that so-called Muslim “activists” such as Umar Khalid were imprisoned because of their religious identity, conveniently ignoring the serious criminal and conspiracy charges against them. The forceful insertion of Khalid’s reference was uncanny but gave the idea what exactly they were trying to do.

Spokesperson Saurav Das went further, describing the charges against Khalid as “false” and “frivolous” and calling his imprisonment a blot on India’s judiciary.

Another CJP spokesperson, Vijeta Dahiya, attempted to reduce the case against Khalid to a speech quoting Mahatma Gandhi and his presence in a WhatsApp group. When questioned about the larger conspiracy case and the more than 50 people killed during the Delhi Riots, Dahiya fell back on the argument that no trial had taken place and accused the journalist questioning him of being “godi media”.
author: AugadhBhudeva

body:
The argument was framed as a defence of due process. Let the trial happen, punish him if he is guilty and release him if he is innocent. However, the same people repeatedly cited the absence of a conviction as proof that the charges were false. They simultaneously demanded that the court process be allowed to conclude and treated the fact that it had not concluded as a declaration of innocence.

The procedural history was also more complicated than the slogan “six years without trial” suggested. Khalid’s latest plea, which was submitted to the court on 6th June, the same day CJP launched its first protest in Delhi, identified itself as his third bail application. His first and second bail applications were dismissed, as were subsequent appeals before the Delhi High Court. His Special Leave Petition was dismissed by the Supreme Court in January 2026, followed by the dismissal of his review petition in April.

The application itself reproduced the Supreme Court’s observation that the case involved several accused persons, voluminous documentary and electronic evidence and accusations concerning a structured and continuing conspiracy. The court also said the record did not show that Umar Khalid and the other accused were in jail only because of prosecution delays or that they had played no role in causing those delays.

While a debate over prolonged pre-trial detention is legitimate in a broader context, in Umar Khalid’s case, the delay in the trial was not caused by the justice system but by the accused themselves. Umar Khalid and the other accused in the larger conspiracy case used every possible tactic to delay the trial and then used the delay as an excuse to seek bail. From repeated bail pleas to pleas seeking to prevent the trial from starting, there was enough evidence to show that India’s justice system was not the culprit behind the six-year-long delay in the trial.

CJP Protestors Called Umar Khalid Their Leader

Support for Khalid was also visible at CJP’s first major protest at Jantar Mantar on 6th June. One protester was filmed declaring, “Umar Khalid is our leader.” Another said that he supported Khalid and saw nothing wrong with doing so. A CJP supporter also described Khalid and Sharjeel Imam as potential future occupants of the country’s highest political offices.

body:
My two cents on what's going to happen in Delhi on Saturday, June 6, 2026.

@abhijeet_dipke, the founder of the @Cockroachisback, has announced to land in Delhi at 0800 Hrs that day. It is unlikely that the Modi govt will try to arrest him there, knowing the massive support the CJP is receiving from all sections of society. I'm not expecting a crowd of thousands to reach the airport to receive him. If they do make it there, the Modi govt will try to scatter them under the pretext of airport security issues. NO FORCE WILL BE USED & NO ARRESTS WILL BE MADE AT THE AIRPORT itself, given the heavy presence of foreign visitors and the world's eyes on this protest.

As per the announced plans, the CJP will then head to the Parliament Street PS to seek permission for a protest later that day at Jantar Mantar. Though JM is a designated space for protests and the police should grant permission, knowing Amit Shah well, the Delhi police will likely deny it, citing law & order issues and protocol rules for applying.

This is where story will unfold. The moment this news breaks, the protestors who have started arriving to join the protest, especially the angry students & Gen-Z masses, might sit in protest anyway. This will trigger a clash between the police and the protestors. The govt might use force against them. This is where they might arrest Abhijeet Dipke under the pretext of inciting the crowd to disrupt law & order and creating unrest in the country. The BJP’s pre-prepared toolkit will be launched to defame the CJP as a foreign-funded entity formed to create civil unrest in India. If that happens, the protest will immediately spread across the country and become the most massive movement since Independence.

If the CJP decides to postpone the protest due to the lack of permission, the Modi govt, together with its 'godi media' & IT cell, will start calling it a failed protest and label Dipke and others 'Darpok'. However, whether or not a clash takes place, the Modi govt will be closely gauging the strength of this online satirical party and the support it receives.

It is unlikely that the protest will be allowed to take place smoothly. Instead, there are chances that the govt may take another route by offering to hold a dialogue and giving false assurances, just as they did during the farmers' and the Ladakh protest. It will be interesting to see on what charges and at what stage they will arrest Abhijeet Dipke to weaken the party and the movement. However, this time it is not just Muslims, farmers, defense personnel, or bankers; it is a charged-up Gen-Z. THINGS ARE DEFINITELY NOT GOING TO BE EASY FOR MODI FROM NOW ON.

So, I suggest everyone joining the protest remain calm and not lose their temper. THE WORLD IS WATCHING. Let them use force if they do; it will only strengthen the storm against this autocratic, shameless govt. To everyone else, whether you are a student, Gen-Z, or a parent; Hindu or Muslim; rich or poor; upper or lower caste; irrespective of your skin color, what you eat, what you wear, or what language you speak, HIT THE ROADS AND JOIN THE MOVEMENT. Those serving as honest bureaucrats, police, and defense forces should also join the protest for the sake of their future generations. If you think the CJP is a fraud, join the protests organized by the Congress party. If you have ideological differences with Congress, join whichever party you support, but protest against this govt. Remember, this is about your future and the future of coming generations.

I'm sure you have read about Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement against the British. There can't be a better way to show a common man's strength to this autocratic, shameless, and failed govt than by protesting and joining a similar non-cooperative movement.

This govt doesn't want you to ask questions; they don't want to be accountable; they don't want you to look them in the eye.

The life of this parrot is only in its eyes. Look into their eyes and ask questions.

body:
The lukewarm response that the Cockroach Janta Party founders are witnessing at Jantar Mantar are the signs of the times we live in. Maasive following on Insta and Fb does not translate into on ground support. The generation which follows you on social media, especially the one's born post 2000, will not be willing to hit the streets. Heck, they are not even willing to walk down the road to get their daily household needs, because Blinkit, Zomato, Swiggy and their fourth friend Amazon, are all there, at their service. 

If only Urban Company and Pronto had an option, where one could hire protestors on one's behalf to protest for a cause, then the dwindling prospects of Cockroach Janta Party would have got a massive boost, but as of now, that functionality is not provided, but you never know.

Second, the faces of this movement lack charisma and public connect. Abhijeet Dipke is no mass leader, like Arvind Kejriwal, his persona and his background does not make the person behind the screen go like 'Woah, he is the guy I am willing to take 1 day off from my office'. 

Saurav Das and the other fellow, who keeps dancing to songs of 1990's Bollywood are not even Twitter celebrities. Also why would the generation following them, born post 2000, vibe to songs of Bollywood movies of 90's and the era of 2000 to 2010.

I did enjoy their dance performance, but then I am not your target audience. Similarly for all of Sonam Wangchuk's achievements, he too is no Anna Hazare and India of 2026, is not India of 2012. Life in India has become more comfortable, while the income disparity remains, both these truths run parallel. 

The issue of NEET, Ethanol are the one's which the ruling government should be rightly questioned about and one can even see supporters of the current government taking them to task on these 2 major issues.

However, the fast unto death emotional blackmail type of protest is passe. It no longer appeals to the current generation, neither to the one's previous to them, who actually grew up watching such protests overturn governments of the day.

A few days back, came across a clip of my friend @Iyervval where he spoke about how we don't realize that how far India has come from the days of abject poverty and this is where the answer to the lack of response to CJP's Dharna Party lies.

More than anything else, it is the lack of imagination on behalf of CJP, and taking a traditional route, which finds itself a lost child in today's comfort at the drop of an app button playstore.

Meanwhile, it is activist and News influencer @tehseenp 's campaign highlighting the issue of Ethanol that is drawing more attention, where in the elected representatives of the day,are being grudingly forced to acknowledge the issue.

May be, just may be, CJP folks study what AIM and Tehseen are saying and take a leaf out of their book.

2026 is not 2012!

body:
History bears witness to the fact that those in power dread nothing more than individuals who ask questions without waving a political flag.

Today, the very youth who ask these uncomfortable questions have taken to the streets. Gathered at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, these young minds are contemptuously being labeled as "TILCHATTE" by some, who are even callously talking about spraying HIT on them.

While the BJP’s frustration is understandable, why the hell are these Congressmen losing their minds and overstepping their bounds? The very youth you are abusing have held up a mirror today to the ruling party, the opposition, and the media alike.
 * **No political stage,**
 * **No constellation of big-shot leaders,**
 * **No electoral rallies,**
 * **No crowds herded into hired buses.**
Yet, thousands of youngsters stood their ground. Most of them were likely sitting on a scorching road, under a blazing sun, without fans or tents, enduring conditions like a furnace for the very first time in their lives.

Those who are undermining them or mocking them are not just insulting these protestors, they are mocking the entire Gen Z and the younger generation of this nation.

These are the very youth who have been raising their voices for years against **unemployment, paper leaks, recruitment scams, inflation, and a compromised media**. Yet, in response, they are mockingly branded as "TILCHATTE."

If this youth quietly tolerates everything, they are hailed as the "future of the nation," but the moment they demand accountability, they are reduced to pests.

When Sonam Wangchuk arrived at the venue, people immediately began painting him as the "New Anna Hazare." Such comparisons are merely a testament to their desperation. Even the Congress is mocking Sonam Wangchuk. They evidently have no respect even for those whom the Modi government jailed simply for speaking up for the betterment of this country.

Some are dismissing this gathering of young citizens as a mere "bubble," claiming that barely 100 to 200 people showed up. To those skeptics, let me say this: deny it all you want, but you cannot escape the reality that this is the boiling wrath of the youth. The anger was always there. Today, it simply erupted and found expression.

Even if it is a passing bubble, the youth desperately need a platform. Their rage and resistance should not be measured by mere headcount, but understood through the depth of their anguish.

The voice that echoed at Jantar Mantar today is not just a protest; it is the restlessness of a generation that no longer wants rhetoric, it demands answers.

Dismissing lakhs of young citizens of this country as "cockroaches" will not make the problems vanish. However, it *will* definitively prove that the establishment has absolutely no answers to their questions.
**Keep questioning.**
**Keep demanding answers.**

Because in a true democracy, a citizen’s greatest weapon will always be their voice.

We were on the ground at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi today as Abhijeet Dipke , founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), addressed hundreds of student protestors and the media. To reclaim the phrase, many students arrived today wearing cockroach masks and holding flowers, demanding systemic accountability for over 1 crore affected students nationwide.

body:
'Deep State' Dipke's Cockroach Protest Stands 
Exposed; Leftist Roaches Crawl Over Jantar Mantar

Roaches roasting under Delhi’s baking sun were roaring one line today — "Cockroaches never fear, never die."

That part is true. But there’s something else about cockroaches they’re not telling you.

Did you know a cockroach can survive without its head? Cut the head off, and it keeps walking for days — on pure instinct. It can’t eat. It can’t think. It just… keeps moving until it starves or rots from the inside.

That is exactly what we are watching today.

June 6, 2026. Jantar Mantar — that sacred feeding ground where India’s professional protestors have dined for decades. 

The Cockroach Janata Party had promised a mega youth revolution. NEET leaks. Exam scams. Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. Twenty-two million algorithm-engineered bots screaming fire across Instagram and X.

The Roach in Chief himself — Abhijeet Dipke — landed fresh off a flight from Boston, constitution in one hand, promises of flowers for the police in the other. They said the streets would burn. 

They said Gen-Z would rise. What actually showed up? A few hundred cockroaches at best. Not even two thousand. Outnumbered by Delhi Police and the bored media crew waiting for a spectacle that never arrived. 

The same old headless wonders – Samajwadi remnants, RJD ruffians, Congress leftovers, AAPtards, and the usual left radicals – are twitching their antennae, desperately sniffing for any scent of chaos.

These political cockroaches had their heads severed in 2014. Electoral heads. Power heads. The constitutional route to power was shut for them — not by any conspiracy, but by the repeated verdict of the Indian people. 

More than a decade out of power with zero realistic hope of returning through the ballot box. So what do they do? They keep twitching. 

They keep marching. They try to reattach their severed heads by plugging into fresh student anger — NEET leaks, exam scams, anything that hurts young people — and then coating that genuine grievance with the same old anarchist poison.

This is not new. This is the exact same script we saw in anti-CAA. The exact same script we saw in the farmers’ protest. Manufacture outrage, import professional andolanjeevis from SFI, AISA, and AISF, bring in the Dafli Gang to beat Umar Khalid-style rhythms, and then pray that the resulting chaos becomes so big that the constitutional order cracks. 

If you cannot win elections, trigger enough street fire that you can usurp power through the back door — exactly as their foreign masters and deep-state scriptwriters have taught them for years.

That is why Abhijeet Dipke flies in from Boston. That is why the same discredited AAPiyas suddenly discover “student outrage". 

That is why Sauraav Das, their spokesperson, lasts ten minutes in the Delhi sun before retreating under a tree with cold coffee in his hand – while still demanding the prime minister's resignation. 

These are not revolutionaries. These are parasites who cannot stand the heat of real sunlight or real accountability.

They keep saying, “We are not a planned party. This is pure students’ outrage.” But the moment the Dafli starts and the old slogans return, the mask slips. 

The same people who spent ten years crying only about Hindu-Muslim politics are now trying to turn every exam paper leak into a constitutional crisis. The hypocrisy is not even clever anymore. It is just pathetic.

And the youth? The real Gen-Z and millennials? They stayed home. Because twenty-two million followers were mostly bots. 

Because the people leading this circus have been discredited so many times that even teenagers can smell the rot. The real students of this country are busy preparing for the next exam, building their futures, and watching India rise — not waiting to be extras in someone else’s failed revolution.

Real accountability on NEET and exam leaks is necessary. Absolutely. But turning every grievance into another prolonged dharna to topple a democratically elected government? The people have seen this movie too many times. They are not buying tickets anymore.

The cockroaches will keep bumbling. They will survive the head cut for a few more days — maybe weeks. They will keep twitching on pure instinct, hoping the next manufactured outrage finally gives them the chaos they need. 

But without real public backing, without electoral legitimacy, without a head – starvation is inevitable. Infection has already begun.

This civilisational nation is not going to let a handful of scurrying roaches feast on manufactured outrage and turn it into unconstitutional anarchy. 

History has it: India does not rise on wishful anarchy. It never will.

The headless march has already begun to die. We are just watching the slow, inevitable end.

body:
An Open Letter to the Jantar Mantar protestors:

My dear young friends,

I address you today not as a politician or an MP, but as someone deeply troubled by what is happening to your generation of young Indians.

This is personal for me. I was born to a middle-class family: my father was a salaried newspaper employee, my mother a homemaker, with three children to educate on one income. For a family like ours, merit was not a slogan. Scholarships, fair examinations, honest results — these were the only way one salary could carry three children's dreams. 

I went to school in Mumbai and Kolkata, to college here in Delhi, topped the University and earned admission into IIM — and chose instead to follow my passion for international affairs, in America, on a scholarship. Nothing was inherited; everything was earned by hard work and yes, Exams.

So I know that a fair, merit-based system is the only ladder for young people from lower and middle-income families to climb up. When that ladder is broken — papers leaked, examinations cancelled, trust destroyed — the children of the rich and powerful do not suffer. They have other ladders. It is your dreams, and your families' sacrifices (and tragically, in some homes, young lives themselves) that are betrayed.

To the young people gathered at Jantar Mantar, and those raising your voices peacefully across India: this country hears you. Your anger is not indiscipline — it is the anguish of a generation that did everything right and was still betrayed . You are not alone.

And to the millions of young Indians watching quietly: your generation is not a problem to be managed. You are the answer to India's future. Do not lose hope. This ladder will be rebuilt — by you, and by every Indian who stands with you.

To Shri Sonam Wangchuk-ji, my heartfelt appeal: please end your fast. You have awakened the conscience of the nation;  that is what a fast is meant to do. India needs your voice for the long road ahead. 

With Parliament in session again from Monday, we will have an opportunity to raise the students’ issues in the highest forum of our democracy. That’s where the problem should be addressed, not by fasting unto death. Please heed my plea. 

And finally, to the Government:  I respectfully urge you to reach out and engage in the dialogue our democracy owes its young citizens. That is not weakness; that is statesmanship.

My two cents on what's going to happen in Delhi on Saturday, June 6, 2026.

@abhijeet_dipke, the founder of the @Cockroachisback, has announced to land in Delhi at 0800 Hrs that day. It is unlikely that the Modi govt will try to arrest him there, knowing the massive support the CJP is receiving from all sections of society. I'm not expecting a crowd of thousands to reach the airport to receive him. If they do make it there, the Modi govt will try to scatter them under the pretext of airport security issues. NO FORCE WILL BE USED & NO ARRESTS WILL BE MADE AT THE AIRPORT itself, given the heavy presence of foreign visitors and the world's eyes on this protest.

As per the announced plans, the CJP will then head to the Parliament Street PS to seek permission for a protest later that day at Jantar Mantar. Though JM is a designated space for protests and the police should grant permission, knowing Amit Shah well, the Delhi police will likely deny it, citing law & order issues and protocol rules for applying.

This is where story will unfold. The moment this news breaks, the protestors who have started arriving to join the protest, especially the angry students & Gen-Z masses, might sit in protest anyway. This will trigger a clash between the police and the protestors. The govt might use force against them. This is where they might arrest Abhijeet Dipke under the pretext of inciting the crowd to disrupt law & order and creating unrest in the country. The BJP’s pre-prepared toolkit will be launched to defame the CJP as a foreign-funded entity formed to create civil unrest in India. If that happens, the protest will immediately spread across the country and become the most massive movement since Independence.

If the CJP decides to postpone the protest due to the lack of permission, the Modi govt, together with its 'godi media' & IT cell, will start calling it a failed protest and label Dipke and others 'Darpok'. However, whether or not a clash takes place, the Modi govt will be closely gauging the strength of this online satirical party and the support it receives.

It is unlikely that the protest will be allowed to take place smoothly. Instead, there are chances that the govt may take another route by offering to hold a dialogue and giving false assurances, just as they did during the farmers' and the Ladakh protest. It will be interesting to see on what charges and at what stage they will arrest Abhijeet Dipke to weaken the party and the movement. However, this time it is not just Muslims, farmers, defense personnel, or bankers; it is a charged-up Gen-Z. THINGS ARE DEFINITELY NOT GOING TO BE EASY FOR MODI FROM NOW ON.

So, I suggest everyone joining the protest remain calm and not lose their temper. THE WORLD IS WATCHING. Let them use force if they do; it will only strengthen the storm against this autocratic, shameless govt. To everyone else, whether you are a student, Gen-Z, or a parent; Hindu or Muslim; rich or poor; upper or lower caste; irrespective of your skin color, what you eat, what you wear, or what language you speak, HIT THE ROADS AND JOIN THE MOVEMENT. Those serving as honest bureaucrats, police, and defense forces should also join the protest for the sake of their future generations. If you think the CJP is a fraud, join the protests organized by the Congress party. If you have ideological differences with Congress, join whichever party you support, but protest against this govt. Remember, this is about your future and the future of coming generations.

I'm sure you have read about Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement against the British. There can't be a better way to show a common man's strength to this autocratic, shameless, and failed govt than by protesting and joining a similar non-cooperative movement.

This govt doesn't want you to ask questions; they don't want to be accountable; they don't want you to look them in the eye.

The life of this parrot is only in its eyes. Look into their eyes and ask questions.

body:
'Deep State' Dipke's Cockroach Protest Stands 
Exposed; Leftist Roaches Crawl Over Jantar Mantar

Roaches roasting under Delhi’s baking sun were roaring one line today — "Cockroaches never fear, never die."

That part is true. But there’s something else about cockroaches they’re not telling you.

Did you know a cockroach can survive without its head? Cut the head off, and it keeps walking for days — on pure instinct. It can’t eat. It can’t think. It just… keeps moving until it starves or rots from the inside.

That is exactly what we are watching today.

June 6, 2026. Jantar Mantar — that sacred feeding ground where India’s professional protestors have dined for decades. 

The Cockroach Janata Party had promised a mega youth revolution. NEET leaks. Exam scams. Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. Twenty-two million algorithm-engineered bots screaming fire across Instagram and X.

The Roach in Chief himself — Abhijeet Dipke — landed fresh off a flight from Boston, constitution in one hand, promises of flowers for the police in the other. They said the streets would burn. 

They said Gen-Z would rise. What actually showed up? A few hundred cockroaches at best. Not even two thousand. Outnumbered by Delhi Police and the bored media crew waiting for a spectacle that never arrived. 

The same old headless wonders – Samajwadi remnants, RJD ruffians, Congress leftovers, AAPtards, and the usual left radicals – are twitching their antennae, desperately sniffing for any scent of chaos.

These political cockroaches had their heads severed in 2014. Electoral heads. Power heads. The constitutional route to power was shut for them — not by any conspiracy, but by the repeated verdict of the Indian people. 

More than a decade out of power with zero realistic hope of returning through the ballot box. So what do they do? They keep twitching. 

They keep marching. They try to reattach their severed heads by plugging into fresh student anger — NEET leaks, exam scams, anything that hurts young people — and then coating that genuine grievance with the same old anarchist poison.

This is not new. This is the exact same script we saw in anti-CAA. The exact same script we saw in the farmers’ protest. Manufacture outrage, import professional andolanjeevis from SFI, AISA, and AISF, bring in the Dafli Gang to beat Umar Khalid-style rhythms, and then pray that the resulting chaos becomes so big that the constitutional order cracks. 

If you cannot win elections, trigger enough street fire that you can usurp power through the back door — exactly as their foreign masters and deep-state scriptwriters have taught them for years.

That is why Abhijeet Dipke flies in from Boston. That is why the same discredited AAPiyas suddenly discover “student outrage". 

That is why Sauraav Das, their spokesperson, lasts ten minutes in the Delhi sun before retreating under a tree with cold coffee in his hand – while still demanding the prime minister's resignation. 

These are not revolutionaries. These are parasites who cannot stand the heat of real sunlight or real accountability.

They keep saying, “We are not a planned party. This is pure students’ outrage.” But the moment the Dafli starts and the old slogans return, the mask slips. 

The same people who spent ten years crying only about Hindu-Muslim politics are now trying to turn every exam paper leak into a constitutional crisis. The hypocrisy is not even clever anymore. It is just pathetic.

And the youth? The real Gen-Z and millennials? They stayed home. Because twenty-two million followers were mostly bots. 

Because the people leading this circus have been discredited so many times that even teenagers can smell the rot. The real students of this country are busy preparing for the next exam, building their futures, and watching India rise — not waiting to be extras in someone else’s failed revolution.

Real accountability on NEET and exam leaks is necessary. Absolutely. But turning every grievance into another prolonged dharna to topple a democratically elected government? The people have seen this movie too many times. They are not buying tickets anymore.

The cockroaches will keep bumbling. They will survive the head cut for a few more days — maybe weeks. They will keep twitching on pure instinct, hoping the next manufactured outrage finally gives them the chaos they need. 

But without real public backing, without electoral legitimacy, without a head – starvation is inevitable. Infection has already begun.

This civilisational nation is not going to let a handful of scurrying roaches feast on manufactured outrage and turn it into unconstitutional anarchy. 

History has it: India does not rise on wishful anarchy. It never will.

The headless march has already begun to die. We are just watching the slow, inevitable end.

body:
An Open Letter to the Jantar Mantar protestors:

My dear young friends,

I address you today not as a politician or an MP, but as someone deeply troubled by what is happening to your generation of young Indians.

This is personal for me. I was born to a middle-class family: my father was a salaried newspaper employee, my mother a homemaker, with three children to educate on one income. For a family like ours, merit was not a slogan. Scholarships, fair examinations, honest results — these were the only way one salary could carry three children's dreams. 

I went to school in Mumbai and Kolkata, to college here in Delhi, topped the University and earned admission into IIM — and chose instead to follow my passion for international affairs, in America, on a scholarship. Nothing was inherited; everything was earned by hard work and yes, Exams.

So I know that a fair, merit-based system is the only ladder for young people from lower and middle-income families to climb up. When that ladder is broken — papers leaked, examinations cancelled, trust destroyed — the children of the rich and powerful do not suffer. They have other ladders. It is your dreams, and your families' sacrifices (and tragically, in some homes, young lives themselves) that are betrayed.

To the young people gathered at Jantar Mantar, and those raising your voices peacefully across India: this country hears you. Your anger is not indiscipline — it is the anguish of a generation that did everything right and was still betrayed . You are not alone.

And to the millions of young Indians watching quietly: your generation is not a problem to be managed. You are the answer to India's future. Do not lose hope. This ladder will be rebuilt — by you, and by every Indian who stands with you.

To Shri Sonam Wangchuk-ji, my heartfelt appeal: please end your fast. You have awakened the conscience of the nation;  that is what a fast is meant to do. India needs your voice for the long road ahead. 

With Parliament in session again from Monday, we will have an opportunity to raise the students’ issues in the highest forum of our democracy. That’s where the problem should be addressed, not by fasting unto death. Please heed my plea. 

And finally, to the Government:  I respectfully urge you to reach out and engage in the dialogue our democracy owes its young citizens. That is not weakness; that is statesmanship.

body:
The lukewarm response that the Cockroach Janta Party founders are witnessing at Jantar Mantar are the signs of the times we live in. Maasive following on Insta and Fb does not translate into on ground support. The generation which follows you on social media, especially the one's born post 2000, will not be willing to hit the streets. Heck, they are not even willing to walk down the road to get their daily household needs, because Blinkit, Zomato, Swiggy and their fourth friend Amazon, are all there, at their service. 

If only Urban Company and Pronto had an option, where one could hire protestors on one's behalf to protest for a cause, then the dwindling prospects of Cockroach Janta Party would have got a massive boost, but as of now, that functionality is not provided, but you never know.

Second, the faces of this movement lack charisma and public connect. Abhijeet Dipke is no mass leader, like Arvind Kejriwal, his persona and his background does not make the person behind the screen go like 'Woah, he is the guy I am willing to take 1 day off from my office'. 

Saurav Das and the other fellow, who keeps dancing to songs of 1990's Bollywood are not even Twitter celebrities. Also why would the generation following them, born post 2000, vibe to songs of Bollywood movies of 90's and the era of 2000 to 2010.

I did enjoy their dance performance, but then I am not your target audience. Similarly for all of Sonam Wangchuk's achievements, he too is no Anna Hazare and India of 2026, is not India of 2012. Life in India has become more comfortable, while the income disparity remains, both these truths run parallel. 

The issue of NEET, Ethanol are the one's which the ruling government should be rightly questioned about and one can even see supporters of the current government taking them to task on these 2 major issues.

However, the fast unto death emotional blackmail type of protest is passe. It no longer appeals to the current generation, neither to the one's previous to them, who actually grew up watching such protests overturn governments of the day.

A few days back, came across a clip of my friend @Iyervval where he spoke about how we don't realize that how far India has come from the days of abject poverty and this is where the answer to the lack of response to CJP's Dharna Party lies.

More than anything else, it is the lack of imagination on behalf of CJP, and taking a traditional route, which finds itself a lost child in today's comfort at the drop of an app button playstore.

Meanwhile, it is activist and News influencer @tehseenp 's campaign highlighting the issue of Ethanol that is drawing more attention, where in the elected representatives of the day,are being grudingly forced to acknowledge the issue.

May be, just may be, CJP folks study what AIM and Tehseen are saying and take a leaf out of their book.

2026 is not 2012!

Anna Hazare ka IAC movement alag time, scale aur organization ka tha – yeh comparison fair nahi. Yeh GenZ satirical movement ka first ground try tha exam leaks pe. Na total flop tha, na blockbuster. Asli judge toh aage ka impact hoga – demands pe asar padta hai ya sirf buzz. Tum kya sochte ho?

body:
Looks like the alleged rumours about #Wangchuk may be right.
Leaders from Ladakh showed little support to Wangchuk since they felt that their issues wrt Ladakh were in discussion with the Centre since long and close to some, if not complete solution.. Challenging the govt now did little to help their cause. 
 
A reluctant #Sonam disappointed with the support, not just at Jantar Mantar but even from Ladakh leaders, is visibly having issues with #Dipke and gang for changing the mood of the protest from - requesting to warning to abusing to manipulating to now turning it visibly political. Also, Dipke and others abandoning wangchuk for hours in the name of meetings, keeping him in the dark and sudden appearances of political leaders on stage without consulting with him has made Wangchuk realise that the protest is not serving his purpose or helping his image.

In all likelihood, wangchuk will pull the plug off his contribution to this naatak mandli very soon in the coming days.
 
There are a lot of cold exchanges happening behind the curtains... The lack of seriousness of the protestors who are more bothered about 'khane mein kya hai' than any concrete cause has also pissed Sonam off. 
He gave a call to #CJP supporters to send recorded videos of 1 day of annshann from home to show support to their #hungerktrike ... Not one came. The disinterest is evident.  

"Yeh hai badlav ka chehra? Khane peene gaane se aage koi kuch karna nahi chahta. Kab tak buffet laga lagakar motivate karenge inhe. Sab pointless hai ." - guess who said that.

🤯 BIG | Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke leads his party to a massive protest on Day-3 at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.

In the video, Dipke can be heard warning the police, who are allegedly seeking Aadhar cards of protestors from the site. Dipke warned them to stop doing that.

In the presence of a massive crowd, Dipke was heard addressing the police.

On the other hand, Dipke was previously heard saying that he would be arrested. However, it has been two days since, and Dipke is still protesting and not being arrested.

Dipke was also heard to have invited farmers to protest and join in the Cockroaches’ movement. However, no farmers have turned out so far.

With the re-NEET examination successfully conducted, Dipke’s protest continues to seek accountability from the Government over the paper leaks.
